CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zutoml parses TOML 1.0 and 1.1 documents into ordinary R values and emits R values as TOML 1.0, with a C99 parser and emitter of its own (no vendored library) over the scalar primitives of zufast (LinkingTo, header-only). It passes the toml-test conformance suite in both directions, types every value by the document’s syntax (never by sniffing strings), and emits deterministic, readable text. Zero hard runtime dependencies: zufast is needed at build time only. It deliberately does not preserve comments or formatting (that is tomledit’s and toml’s job), validate against a schema, or offer a C API.

Two documents outrank this file. .agents/design.md is the specification, numbered §1–§20: every statement in it is a decision, and open questions live only in its §18. .agents/roadmap.md sequences it into Stages 0–8, each with a Status: line under its heading. Both were adopted on 2026-10-08 from RFC 0004 in pedrobtz/packages. CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides, the roadmap sequences.

It is a member of the zu* family (sibling checkouts in ../). zuyaml is the model for the R API shape and the bigint class, zujson for the array lattice, zucbor for limits, conditions, the conformance runner and the mutation check, zuxml for R/zu_source.R. When a question is not answered here or in the design, look at how those packages settle it before inventing something new.

Current state

0.1.0 is on CRAN, published 2026-11-07 (crandb, verified 2026-11-11). Every stage of the roadmap is done. toml_validate(), toml_parse() (with positions = and select =), toml_read(), toml_emit(), toml_write(), the markers toml_inline(), toml_literal() and toml_multiline(), toml_bigint() and zutoml_info() are exported, with a vignette. Every toml-test case of TOML 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 passes in both directions (D17: 1.1.0 is read by default; the emitter writes 1.0.0). The review in #29 is fixed: the emitter checks the invariants R does not enforce (data frame shape, finite dates and times, canonical wall-clock text, a factor’s NA level), so everything it returns is valid TOML 1.0.0, and data_frame = TRUE is linear in the cells.

On 2026-11-11 DESCRIPTION on main still says Version: 0.1.0: the 0.1.0.9000 bump has not landed, and no 0.1.0 tag exists. There is no cran-release.yaml, so neither happens by itself.

Update this section at the end of every stage: what exists, what is next, and the date.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #44, v0.1.1. The v0.1.0 parent was #1, with sub-issues #2 (Stage 0) to #10 (Stage 8), plus #21 (7b) and #24 (7c): the roadmap has eleven stages, 0 to 8 and 7b and 7c, added after Stage 7. A stage’s status goes in its Status: line, never in its heading, because that would change the anchor every issue links to.

zutoml depends on one sibling, LinkingTo: zufast (>= 0.1.0), from CRAN since 2026-10-21. A release build is checked against zufast’s CRAN tarball, not a newer checkout, because header-only is source-compatible, not ABI-compatible. No package depends on zutoml.

Commands

The check this package runs, rather than the plain one:

_R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_=0 Rscript -e 'devtools::check(cran = TRUE)'

Install zufast from CRAN, or from the sibling checkout (R CMD INSTALL ../zufast) to try an unreleased change. roxygen2 must be 8.1.0 or newer (Config/roxygen2/version); an older one rewrites man/.

Gate scripts, run from the package root, each with the roadmap stage that added it and the workflow that runs it:

Script Stage What it does
tools/update-fixtures 0 fetch toml-test at the pinned tag, write the manifest
tools/run-conformance 1 every toml-test case through the check phase (conformance)
tools/run-fuzz [secs] 1 canary first, then fuzz_parse under ASan+UBSan (hardening)
tools/run-lint 1 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Werror on project C
tools/check-symbols <so> 1 only R_init_zutoml exported; no stdio, abort, exit, assert
tools/run-mutation-check 3 every check-phase /* GUARD */ seen to be load-bearing (40)
tools/run-mutation-check-r 6 the build phase’s and emitter’s guards, through R (8)
tools/check-no-network 6 no test opens a URL or socket
tools/run-benchmarks 7 parse vs RcppTOML, emit vs zuyaml; not a CI gate

tools/run-fuzz needs a clang with libFuzzer; on macOS, Homebrew’s: FUZZ_CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang. Run tools/check-symbols on an R CMD INSTALL build, not a load_all() one (load_all() compiles with -UNDEBUG).

Architecture

R/            parse.R, data-frame.R, read.R, select.R, validate.R, emit.R
              (toml_emit, toml_write), markers.R, classes.R (toml_bigint),
              conditions.R, args.R, info.R, tokens.R (the lexer's token
              table, internal), zu_source.R (copied verbatim from zuxml;
              edit there), zutoml-package.R
src/          init.c                      registration only
              ztm_r.c, ztm_r.h            .Call entry points and SEXP glue
              ztm_check.h                 the check phase's R-free interface:
                                          tokens, values, the node tree
              ztm_lex.c, ztm_parse.c      check phase: lexer, grammar, table
                                          model, limits
              ztm_value.c                 scalars: TOML shape checks, then
                                          zufast; string decoding
              ztm_status.c                enumerator names (R-free)
              ztm_build.c, ztm_build.h    build phase: §6 mapping, positions,
                                          select; ztm_mkchar() the one
                                          CHARSXP site
              ztm_emit.c, ztm_emit.h      §7, §8
              Makevars                    hand-listed OBJECTS, $(C_VISIBILITY)
fuzz/         fuzz_parse.c, fuzz_canary.c, probe.c (the mutation check's
              driver), arena.c, toml.dict (not in the tarball)
tools/        the gate scripts above
tests/testthat/toml-test/   the suite at a pinned tag, with manifest.tsv
              (not under fixtures/: the 100-byte path limit; not in the
              tarball, see Testing)

The pipeline is: validate and decode the input in R → check phase (ztm_lex.c, ztm_parse.c, ztm_value.c: pure C, R-free behind ztm_check.h; UTF-8, tokens with positions, the table model, scalars through zufast, the limits; produces the node tree ztm_doc) → build phase (ztm_build.c: R values and the lattice from the node tree, sizes from the check’s counts) → R value. Local date-times reach the session’s zone in R/parse.R; data frames are built in R/data-frame.R. toml_validate() is the check phase alone. The emitter, src/ztm_emit.c, is a separate one-pass path into an R_alloc() buffer, with R/emit.R turning local POSIXct into wall-clock text first.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • The check phase contains no R. ztm_lex.c, ztm_parse.c and ztm_status.c never include R.h; scratch, interrupts and “no offset” go through the hooks in ztm_check.h. The fuzz build (-DZTM_STANDALONE) compiles them standalone, and that is the only reason the fuzz gate works.
  • No R object is allocated before the check has passed over the whole document, and container sizes come from the check’s counts, never from the input (design §4, rule 1).
  • toml_validate() is exactly toml_parse()’s check phase: same code, same limits. The only disagreements are the §6.4 unrepresentable cases, and a test enumerates them.
  • C never calls Rf_error(). Entry points return a status by enumerator name; R/conditions.R maps names to classes. R maps by name, never by matching English.
  • Everything the C holds is R_alloc()ed or PROTECTed, so there are no finalizers and no cleanup paths; any hook may longjmp from anywhere. Do not introduce malloc() without reading design §13.
  • zufast parses digits, not TOML. The lexer checks TOML’s shape (underscores between digits, no sign before a prefix, seconds present, ±hh:mm only), strips prefixes and underscores, then calls zuf_parse_i64_opt() with base, zuf_parse_f64() or zuf_parse_datetime(), and checks r.ptr == last. zufast’s grammars are wider than TOML’s in every case; skipping the shape check makes zutoml accept documents toml-test says are invalid.
  • Security guards carry a /* GUARD: name */ marker on their if line and have a toml-test invalid case or a hostile input; tools/run-mutation-check proves each is load-bearing. Add both for any new guard.
  • The emitter charges max_depth as the parser does, so it never writes what the parser refuses (design §8).
  • Three decoder rules make toml_emit(toml_parse(d)) reproduce d and are pinned by the round-trip tests: a one-element array decodes as an I() value, booleans do not join the numbers, and whole doubles emit as integers.
  • ztm_mkchar() is the only place a CHARSXP is made, so the U+0000 and length guards cannot drift between values, names and keys.
  • Portable make only in src/Makevars: OBJECTS hand-listed, no $(wildcard), no $(shell), no -W* overrides, no Makevars.win.
  • A change to a contract amends the design in the same commit: the exports, the mapping tables, the limits, the condition fields. Design §6–§7, the roxygen tables and the tests are the same table three times.

Naming

Layer Prefix Examples
R exports toml_ plus zutoml_info() toml_parse(), toml_emit(), toml_bigint()
R condition classes zutoml_ zutoml_error, zutoml_parse_error
User-facing value class toml_ toml_bigint
R and C internals ztm_ / ZTM_ ztm_mkchar(), ZTM_STANDALONE
.Call entry points zutoml_ zutoml_parse
Test-switching variables ZUTOML_ ZUTOML_SKIP_HEAVY, ZUTOML_SLOW_TESTS

zu_/ZU_ is zukomp’s family-wide C prefix; zuf_, zb_, zuc_, zux_, zuh_ are taken. Stage 0 verified that ztm_ was free.

Editing rules specific to zutoml

  • There is no README.Rmd, a deviation from the shared rule: edit README.md directly and keep its example output in step with the code by running it.
  • Prose is en-GB (Language: en-GB); domain terms go in inst/WORDLIST.
  • Suggests only: zujson for the suite’s expectation files, withr, testthat, knitr, rmarkdown.
  • Every exported function has @return and runnable @examples.
  • R/zu_source.R is copied verbatim from ../zuxml; fix it there and re-copy. air.toml excludes it from air format.
  • NEWS.md keeps a versioned heading (# zutoml 0.1.0.9000): a bare “development version” heading is a check NOTE once it is the only one.

Testing

  • No file-scope objects, because shuffle = TRUE reorders a file’s top-level code too. Anything two tests share goes in helper-*.R.
  • Assert on condition classes and fields: expect_error(..., class = "zutoml_parse_error") plus kind, line, column, offset or path.
  • Serial. No Config/testthat/parallel, so gctorture and valgrind see the C.
  • The conformance suite is toml-test (MIT; v2.2.0 on 2026-10-08), fetched only by tools/update-fixtures into tests/testthat/toml-test/ with a manifest, never hand-edited. It is in git but .Rbuildignored, so no file by another author ships and Authors@R names only the maintainer. toml_test_dir() skips the tests that read it where it is absent (R CMD check on a tarball, on CRAN and in CI alike); tools/run-conformance and devtools::test() run them from the checkout, and the conformance workflow does so in CI. Its tagged JSON expectations are compared type by type against toml_parse(d, simplify = "none") twice: with datetimes = "keep", and with datetimes = "convert", local_time = "difftime" (only the second tells a date from a string). It does not cover the lattice, data_frame =, the limits or the hostile inputs, which are the package’s own tests.
  • Helpers in tests/testthat/:
    • helper-expect.R: expect_toml() (emit gives exactly this text), expect_roundtrip(), expect_zutoml_error() (class plus kind).
    • helper-fixtures.R: toml_test_dir(), toml_test_cases(), tagged_json_to_r(), toml_test_diff(), tested in test-helper-fixtures.R.
    • helper-generate.R: random values for the round-trip properties, built to avoid exactly the losses design §7.4 lists, so a difference is a bug.
    • helper-lex.R: token and lexer-error helpers over the internal ztm_tokens().
    • helper-select.R: the document test-select.R reads.
    • helper-skip.R: skip_heavy() on ZUTOML_SKIP_HEAVY, set by the gctorture and valgrind legs; skip_if_no_slow_tests() on ZUTOML_SLOW_TESTS; skip_until_exported().
  • Never write an expected double as a long decimal literal: R’s parser on macOS arm64 rounds some to a neighbouring double. Use exact forms (2^53, -2^63) or bits.
  • Time budget: under 15 s. The 10^6-element hostile inputs call skip_heavy().
  • Done, beyond the shared definition: gctorture(TRUE) clean when C changed, and a gate counts only once it has been seen to fail.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml@v1. A deviation from ci.md: it does not pass profile: auto. It runs the quick profile on a pull request and the full profile on every push to main and under full-ci. It adds a Windows R-devel row to the shared runners (CRAN’s Windows R-devel flavour) and sets nosuggests and nold (CRAN’s NOSUGGESTS and NOLD flavours), both full profile only.
  • coverage.yaml calls coverage.yml, pinned by commit (it holds a write token), and writes the badge under .github/badges/.
  • pkgdown.yaml builds the site.
  • native-checks.yaml calls sanitizers.yml (UBSan on clang and gcc, ASan with -UNDEBUG), valgrind.yml, lto.yml, gctorture.yml, analyzers.yml and rchk.yml, weekly on Wednesday as well as on push. It still skips prose with a paths-ignore list rather than the changes.yml gate.
  • conformance.yaml (own) checks that the committed suite equals a fresh fetch at the pinned tag, runs every case for TOML 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 through tools/run-conformance, and has toml_emit()’s text for every valid case accepted by toml-test’s reference decoder (BurntSushi/toml, pinned) and by Python’s tomllib.
  • hardening.yaml (own) runs the C-boundary gates: lint, symbols, both mutation checks, no network, and libFuzzer over the check phase with the corpus cached between runs (2 minutes per pull-request push, 30 minutes nightly).

Neither of the package’s own workflows calls changes.yml yet, so a label does not skip them. Dependabot updates github-actions. Nothing is vendored, so there is no vendor.yaml.
